transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-15 14:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Maria Torres (Lakeside Head of AI), Sam Patel (Lakeside Eng Lead), Jordan Lee (Lakeside SecOps)

Summary (auto): quick console tour, deep dive into per-route cost analytics, discuss pilot data and security docs.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll run through the console analytics piece and show how you can do per route breakdowns, cost, and the optimization recommendations.
[00:15] Dr. Maria Torres: great thanks Alex, we've got about 45 minutes, really keen to see how per-route visibility looks — we run a bunch of small routing decisions in prod so understanding the hot routes is critical.
[00:28] Priya Singh: hi team, I'll drive the demo, Alex will chime on pricing and commercial, and happy to answer architecture questions. Quick call out: i might mispronounce a few names, transcription may be rough.
[00:40] Priya Singh: opening the Console now, first screen is the Usage Analytics — top left is total tokens by day, top right you can filter by route, model, and env. if i click "Routes" it surfaces the list of active endpoints and percent of traffic.
[01:05] Sam Patel: can you show us the triage route? we call it "symptom-triage-v2" in our infra.
[01:12] Priya Singh: sure — typing — hmm i see a route called symp-triage-v2, looks like 22% of traffic, avg latency 320ms, cost per 1k tokens $0.42 in hosted tier. note the model variant is redwood-3b-quant, which is a lower cost path.
[01:35] Dr. Maria Torres: cost per 1k tokens, is that net of batching? how do you factor streaming vs non-streaming?
[01:44] Priya Singh: good question, the console shows raw consumed tokens and then the modeled cost given your pricing tier. batching reduces per-token compute cost — we surface a modeled "effective cost" if you enable continuous batching. streaming has additional small overhead but is mostly I/O. this is an approximation, for pilot we recommend running our benchmark to get actual numbers.
[02:12] Alex Chen: and to add, if you go Dedicated the per-token number is different — your reserved capacity commit will lower unit costs but you trade off with committed spend.
[02:25] Jordan Lee: on security, how does this analytics pipeline handle PII? does logs retain raw prompts?
[02:33] Priya Singh: in hosted default we redact PII in logs and we keep a configurable retention; for Private or Dedicated you can opt to disable retention or ship logs to your S3/VPC. we also have KMS integrations for encryption at rest and SAML SSO for access control.
[02:54] Alex Chen: i'll follow-up with the SOC2 packet and the audit log specifics.
[03:00] Priya Singh: jumping back to per-route dashboards — click into a route and you get token histogram, latency percentiles, error rates, and cost waterfall. the waterfall breaks down compute cost, kv-cache hits, and infra overhead. disclaimer: sometimes the transcribe shows KV cache as K V cash, we see that in older transcripts.
[03:25] Sam Patel: kv-cache hits — how are those counted and what's configurable?
[03:29] Priya Singh: it's based on the prefix caching heuristic; we surface cache hit ratio and estimated savings. you can set ttl and prefix keys in your route config to tune it. for stateful chat flows we recommend enabling prefix caching to reduce per-token compute.
[03:47] Dr. Maria Torres: do you show per-customer or per-user breakdowns? we need to audit by tenant.
[03:53] Priya Singh: yes, you can filter by customer_id header or user_id and create saved views. RBAC applies so only authorized roles can see PII-linked breakdowns.
[04:10] Alex Chen: question for the team — what's your monthly token volume and rough route distribution?
[04:15] Sam Patel: at the moment we average 120M tokens/month and top 5 routes are triage, intake-form, search-enhance, chart-summarize, and patient-message. triage is about 40% of usage.
[04:30] Priya Singh: ok that's helpful — on the console i can show a "Top N routes" report and the cost by route. here you can export to CSV or link the view to a dashboard for stakeholders.
[04:50] Dr. Maria Torres: when you say cost by route, is that just tokens times price or do you simulate batching impacts?
[04:57] Priya Singh: we show both: nominal cost (tokens * list price) and adjusted cost which factors in estimated batching efficiency and cache savings. the adjusted cost uses your request size distribution to estimate batching gains.
[05:18] Alex Chen: and if you'd like we can run a short benchmark using a sample of your traffic to estimate real-world delta. that's typically the pilot phase.
[05:30] Sam Patel: what's involved in the benchmark? we have some concerns about sharing live PII.
[05:36] Priya Singh: benchmark can be run either with anonymized samples or synthetically generated prompts; we provide a checklist (we'll share) that lists required fields: route names, avg prompt length, avg response tokens, concurrency targets. we also accept anonymized payloads into a secure bucket.
[05:58] Jordan Lee: about compliance — which controls do you provide for audit logs and key rotation?
[06:05] Alex Chen: we have audit trails for API calls, role changes, and deployment rollouts. key rotation via KMS is supported and we can integrate with your rotation schedule. i'll include specifics in the SOC2 packet.
[06:20] Priya Singh: switching to Optimize tab — recommendations engine surfaces model/quantization suggestions per route, and a "what-if" slider to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs. you can apply suggestions and schedule a canary rollout.
[06:40] Dr. Maria Torres: can the console simulate tradeoffs per-route? eg keep triage on low-latency but move other routes to quantized cheaper models?
[06:48] Priya Singh: yes, the per-route policy UI lets you pin models and set fallback variants; you can say triage -> prioritize latency (no quantization), intake-form -> prioritize cost (quantized). the cost model will then re-run and show expected monthly savings.
[07:10] Sam Patel: curious about streaming and function calling costs — we use function calls to pull patient records. is that modeled?
[07:17] Priya Singh: function calls add a small per-call overhead in the cost model — we surface it separately in the waterfall as "I/O overhead".
[07:26] Dr. Maria Torres: ok good. any notes on private deployments? we might need a VPC option for PHI.
[07:33] Alex Chen: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem, with customer-managed networking and strict data residency. we can discuss pricing for Private separately — typically an enterprise contract.
[07:45] Priya Singh: back to the analytics, here's an anomalies panel — it flags routes with sudden token surges or latency regressions and links to example requests. it's helpful for regressions after a model rollout.
[08:05] Sam Patel: love that — can we export those alerts to pager duty?
[08:10] Priya Singh: yes, alerting hooks to PagerDuty/Slack/Webhook are supported.
[08:18] Dr. Maria Torres: any known gotchas with the console? we've seen dashboards undercount tokens in other vendors.
[08:25] Priya Singh: we try to surface raw ingestion tokens and our billing tokens (which include rounding rules). occasionally short streaming fragments can be misattributed; we have a reconciliation report in the Billing export. for pilot we'll run a reconciliation together.
[08:45] Alex Chen: to recap next steps: i'll send SOC2 and pricing; Priya will share benchmark checklist and a sample dashboard export; Lakeside to provide token counts and route list.
[08:58] Dr. Maria Torres: sounds good. one more ask — can you include a sample SSO user role mapping?
[09:05] Alex Chen: yes we'll include role mapping suggestions for Admin/Viewer/Operator and the RBAC matrix.
[09:12] Priya Singh: ok i'll also attach a short how-to doc for per-route cost tuning — TTLs, prefix caching, and batch sizing.
[09:25] Sam Patel: thanks for the demo — this was helpful.
[09:28] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll get the files to you this week.
[09:33] Alex Chen: thanks everyone — talk soon.
